name: As Fast As Possible
description: On vacations n pupils decided to go on excursion and gather all together. They need to overcome the path with the length l meters. Each of the pupils will go with the speed equal to v 1 . To get to the excursion quickly, it was decided to rent a bus, which has seats for k people (it means that it can't fit more than k people at the same time) and the speed equal to v 2 . In order to avoid seasick, each of the pupils want to get into the bus no more than once . Determine the minimum time required for all n pupils to reach the place of excursion. Consider that the embarkation and disembarkation of passengers, as well as the reversal of the bus, take place immediately and this time can be neglected.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains five positive integers n , l , v 1 , v 2 and k ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 000 , 1 ≤ l ≤ 10 9 , 1 ≤ v 1 < v 2 ≤ 10 9 , 1 ≤ k ≤ n ) — the number of pupils, the distance from meeting to the place of excursion, the speed of each pupil, the speed of bus and the number of seats in the bus.
output_specification: Print the real number — the minimum time in which all pupils can reach the place of excursion. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error won't exceed 10 - 6 .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 700A — As Fast As Possible [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
